After aggressively expanding its real estate footprint in the South Bay region in 2025, Apple is once again enlarging its presence in Sunnyvale. Details below.

Apple continues to expand its footprint

According to the Mercury News (via AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease a 125,800-square-foot office building at 580 North Mary Avenue in Sunnyvale.

This deal marks Apple's first major real estate transaction in the area in 2026. Prior to this, the company spent over US$1 billion expanding its South Bay footprint in 2025, with one move after another.

The expansion included: purchasing a three-building complex known as the Gateway in Cupertino for US$166.9 million, acquiring the two-building Mathilda Commons campus in Sunnyvale for US$350 million, and buying the adjacent four-building Mathilda Campus for US$365 million.

Apple subsequently spent another US$216 million to acquire two buildings along Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its total expansion in the Bay Area in 2025 to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space.

Returning to the newly signed lease, the Mercury News pointed out that this deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay region begins to pick up again, with vacancy rates improving compared to the previous quarter and the same period last year:

According to a Colliers report, the office vacancy rate in the South Bay region was 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines the market area as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

The report also noted that, apart from Apple, Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Way in Sunnyvale.
